title: Crash recovery: resolving what a dead supervisor left
note: Every mutation here either strands work forever or reclaims a lease somebody still holds -- the two failures that sit either side of the same decision. UNKNOWN is the load-bearing case: a record from another host is not evidence the holder is dead, and a mutation that collapses UNKNOWN into GONE puts two workers on one task, which is exactly what a lease exists to prevent. The recovery mutations that move a task FORWARD are the tempting ones: the execution record says the process exited 0, and completing it anyway is a recovery process finishing another party's work under a lease nobody holds. V11 was REMOVED as equivalent rather than left as a false finding: a task cannot reach LEASED or EXECUTING without a lease, because that edge carries requires_lease and replay re-authorizes it, so the branch guarding against it cannot differ. The assumption is asserted by a test rather than left in a comment.

mutations.name: V1_an_unknown_holder_counts_as_gone
mutations.find:
if not here or not recorded.host_boot_id:
        # One side cannot say which boot it is from, so nothing about the
        # pid is safe to conclude.
        return UNKNOWN
mutations.replace:
if not here or not recorded.host_boot_id:
        return GONE
mutations.rationale: a record that cannot say which boot it came from authorises a reclaim, so a live holder on another host is declared dead and two workers run one task

mutations.name: V2_a_pid_with_no_start_time_counts_as_alive
mutations.rationale: an unidentifiable pid is treated as the recorded process, so a REUSED pid keeps a dead holder's lease alive forever

mutations.name: V3_pid_reuse_is_not_detected
mutations.find: return ALIVE if now == recorded.start_ticks else GONE
mutations.rationale: any process occupying the number counts as the one that took the lease; the work is stranded behind an impostor

mutations.name: V4_a_reboot_does_not_invalidate_recorded_pids
mutations.rationale: pids recorded before a reboot are looked up against the new boot, where the same numbers belong to unrelated processes

mutations.name: V5_the_boot_id_is_invented_when_unavailable
mutations.find:
except OSError:                                  # pragma: no cover
        return ""
mutations.replace:
except OSError:                                  # pragma: no cover
        return "synthetic"
mutations.rationale: a synthesised id compares unequal across processes on the same boot, so every record looks stale and every recovery becomes a reclaim

mutations.name: V6_stat_is_split_on_whitespace
mutations.rationale: a process whose name contains ')' shifts every later field, so start time is read from the wrong column and a live process looks reused

mutations.name: V7_recovery_never_asks_the_operating_system
mutations.rationale: the sequence number is the only expiry again, so a crashed supervisor's task is stranded forever -- the gap this closes

mutations.name: V8_recovery_reclaims_a_live_lease
mutations.rationale: every in-flight task is reclaimed regardless of who holds it, which is a second worker rather than a recovery

mutations.name: V9_recovery_completes_the_task_from_its_own_record
mutations.find:
moved = self._move(task, TaskState.QUEUED, actor,
                               TaskRole.SYSTEM, note=why)
mutations.replace:
moved = self._move(
                task,
                TaskState.COMPLETED if ran else TaskState.QUEUED,
                actor, TaskRole.SYSTEM, note=why)
mutations.rationale: a recovery process finishes another party's work under a lease nobody holds, which is the ownership bypass the lease exists to prevent

mutations.name: V10_a_completed_task_is_dragged_back_to_the_queue
mutations.rationale: work awaiting an independent verifier is requeued and re-run, discarding a finished result rather than having it checked

mutations.name: V12_the_lease_does_not_record_its_holders_process
mutations.rationale: nothing later can ask whether the holder is still there, so recovery is back to a sequence number that stopped advancing

mutations.name: V13_recovery_is_not_run_before_a_governed_run
mutations.find:
self.recover()

        # THE DUPLICATE CHECK COMES FIRST, before a task exists.
mutations.replace: # THE DUPLICATE CHECK COMES FIRST, before a task exists.
mutations.rationale: recovery has no production caller, so the mechanism exists and nothing invokes it -- the defect class this whole row is about

mutations.name: V14_expired_leases_are_no_longer_consulted
mutations.rationale: the ordinary lapsed-lease case stops being recovered; only the process-liveness path remains, which does not cover a holder on another host
